PythonRef.description:
Python link code: a file under the project's ``.specto/links/`` and an entry point
that returns the output data (JSON), by ``resolves_to``:

- ``table``: ``entry(items, params, root)`` returns ``{source key: output value}``,
  looked up by the source's picked key;
- ``samples``: ``entry(items, params, root)`` returns ``[[number, value], ...]``, the
  nearest number to the source's time picks;
- ``value`` (per pick, #168): ``entry(value, items, params, root)`` returns the output
  value for the source's current value, and runs again (debounced) whenever that
  value changes. The value as the script sees it: files ``{root, paths}``, selection
  ``{keys, last}``, time a number of seconds, any other port its JSON.

``items`` are the source view's collection items (key, parts, meta; empty when the
source has none, a file tree), ``params`` the link's params, ``root`` the project
folder. Every output value is converted to the ``output`` port type: files from
``{root?, paths}`` or a list of paths; selection from a key, a list of keys or
``{keys, last?}``; content from ``{root?, paths}`` or a list of paths (the files are
read; a folder stands for its readable files, a map's for its GeoJSON) or ``{root?,
entries}``; time from a number of seconds; collection (a view's whole data, built as
an intaker would) from ``{root?, items}`` or a list of items, an item a path or
``{key?, parts: {role: path} | [path, ...], keys?, meta?}``. ADR 0016: it runs at
resolve time (when the file, the params, the source collection or, per pick, the
value change), never per frame; ADR 0006: only
after the user approved the file's exact content in the window (the view's Approve, or
the approval card a ``link.approve`` request opens; the command itself never approves,
#203), and out of
process.

resolves_to.title: Resolves To

output.description: The port type of the resolved values.
output.title: Output

guide.per_pick: resolves_to: "value" means per pick: the source's current value is part of the resolve key, and the script returns the output value itself. Signature: entry(value, items, params, root). It runs out of process for each new value of the source (debounced: a burst of picks runs only the last). With no source value yet, the script does not run (the link waits). This is the link for anything an intaker, follow or read_contents link cannot express: a mapping between folders, a lookup across files, a join.
guide.table_and_samples: resolves_to: table | samples keep entry(items, params, root): {source key: output value} looked up by the picked key, or [[number, output value], ...] picked by the nearest number.

value.files: {"root": "<abs folder>", "paths": ["rel/posix", ...] | null}. null means the whole folder (project.all_files). A file tree's picks expand folders to files.

guide.items: the source view's collection items (empty for a file tree)

returns.files: {"root"?, "paths": [...]} or ["path", ...] becomes a FilesValue. root defaults to the project root; a relative root joins it. (No view has a files input today: nothing takes a files output yet.)
returns.selection: "key" | ["k1", "k2"] | {"keys": [...], "last"?} becomes a Selection. last defaults to the last key.
returns.content: {"root"?, "paths": [...]} or ["path", ...] reads those files into a ContentValue. A folder expands to its readable files (for a map, its GeoJSON files only); geojson/json/text are told apart by extension. Alternatively {"root"?, "entries": [...]} is taken as is. A map target needs geojson entries, else a fix-it.
returns.time: a number or {"t", "timeline"?} becomes a TimeValue. With no timeline it is the target's own (a video's, a usd stage's, a gallery's clock).
returns.camera: {position, target, ...} becomes a CameraValue (the 3d view's frame, Y up; a usd view takes it too).
returns.collection: a view's whole data, built as an intaker builds it: {"root"?, "items": [...]} or a list of items. An item is a path, or {"key"?, "parts": {"<role>": "<path>"} or ["<path>", ...], "keys"?: {field: value}, "meta"?: {...}}. Paths are relative to root (the project folder) or absolute, and must exist; a part listed without a role gets its extension (.jpg) as the role. The key defaults to the first part's path without extension, keys to {stem: key}; keys must be unique. Each part is recorded with its relative path and stat, so a file tree lists it, a 3d view gets its scene, and the same result is not delivered twice. Feeds any view's data input (gallery, file tree, markdown, 3d, usd, ...).
returns.null: nothing is delivered (the target keeps what it has). [] clears a selection.

guide.status: canvas.state's links[<id>] is {state, message} (waiting, resolving, resolved, failed, needs_approval; path and hash for a python link). A failed run's message is one line (<path>:<entry>: <error>, or the fix-it for a wrong shape); trace is the script's own traceback (its frames only, paths relative to the project): read it to fix the code. A failure stays until the code, the params or the source value change; a run longer than 120 s fails and is killed. The code runs as python -I -X utf8 (files are UTF-8; print goes to a log, not the result) and sees only the app's installed packages.
guide.fix_it: a wrong shape fails the link with "<path>:<entry> returned <value> for a <type> output; return <shapes>", the shapes being these per type

shapes.selection: a key, a list of keys or {"keys": [...], "last"?: ...}
shapes.content: the files to read as {"paths": [...]} or a list of paths, or {"entries": [...]}
shapes.collection: {"root"?: ..., "items": [...]} or a list of items; an item is a path or {"key"?: ..., "parts": {"<role>": "<path>"} or ["<path>", ...], "keys"?: {...}}

guide.map: a map's features input takes content and shows GeoJSON files, not inline data: feed it tree B's selected_files through read_contents, or return the .geojson paths or their folders ({"paths": [...]}) from a python link with output content. A map fed non-GeoJSON says "<path>:<entry>: the map shows GeoJSON files, but <file> is <format>; return the .geojson paths or their folders"
guide.trees: a file tree's data input is a collection (an intaker), not files; its selection input (keys: relative paths of files or folders) selects and reveals them and sends their files on selected_files. No follow link works between two trees: drive a second tree with a per-pick python link (output selection) into its selection input.
guide.code: write the file with write_link_code {name, code} as .specto/links/<name>.py, then submit the python link on it in one submit; the code runs only after the user approves its exact content (the view's Approve button); any change to the file needs approval again. read_link_code shows the code and whether it is approved. Plain Python 3 and its standard library, JSON in and out; it must return quickly (it runs per pick).

example.prompt: picking a world in the file tree selects its source folder in a second tree, and a map shows that folder's GeoJSONs
example.chain: tree A.selected_files -> python "value" (output selection) -> tree B.selection (recordings/<session>/<clip>/... -> annotations/<session>/<clip>/geo). Then tree B.selected_files -> read_contents (or python "value", output content) -> map.features.

view_types.label: Gallery
view_types.doc: Drag-to-pan, wheel-zoom tile gallery of a collection of any kind (images; video poster frames, first pdf pages, text excerpts, 3D kind icons); native Qt Quick item.

view_types.label: JSON inspector
view_types.doc: Monaco read-only JSON view with folding and outline; shows the selected item of its collection.

view_types.label: Scratch pad
view_types.doc: The project's scratch pad, at most one per canvas: named pages (tabs) of markdown, each one file .specto/scratch/<page>.md, rendered like the markdown view (outline, zoom) and editable in place (a rendered / source toggle, autosaved). What the user drops or pastes (Ctrl+V) from any view or another app is appended as markdown: text as text, pictures embedded from <page>.assets/, files and prims as links relative to the page, an item from a view as a short quote with its source. You read and edit pages with scratch_read, scratch_append and scratch_write. Every change is an undo step. A source of its own: it needs no input link and counts as reachable from the project. The page shown (params.page) goes out on items (the page's markdown, then the files and pictures it links: a gallery or preview can follow it); a link the user clicks goes out on selection and shows in the pad's preview beside it.

page.description: The page shown and sent out on items, by id (p2) or name; the pad's active page when left out. Clicking a tab sets it.

summary.sentence: The gallery shows the scratch pad's items.

view_types.label: USD
view_types.doc: One OpenUSD stage (.usd, .usda, .usdc, .usdz), read-only: the picked item of its collection (or the first), stepping through the rest. Rendered out of process: RTX (ovrtx) when this machine has the ovrtx capability, otherwise Hydra Storm. Navigation as in the 3d view: camera_mode free (Unreal Editor's: drag turns and walks, right-drag looks and WASD flies, middle-drag pans, wheel dollies, Alt+drag orbits) or orbit (drag orbits the selection or the point under it, middle-drag pans, right-drag and wheel dolly toward it); F frames the selected prims' whole subtrees, else everything; a click selects the prim under the cursor and sends <item key>#<prim path> out; content is the selected prim's properties. Time is the stage's timecodes in seconds; camera is shared with the 3d view. Nothing is written to the file.

renderer.description: auto: on Windows and Linux, rtx when this machine has the ovrtx capability, otherwise storm (Hydra Storm, any GPU, no RTX look); on macOS always storm. describe view:usd reports renderer_auto, what auto runs here.

mode.description: RTX render mode: rt real-time path tracing, pt path tracing (accumulates while nothing moves), minimal. Ignored by storm.

look_through.description: A camera prim path of the stage to look through, or null for the free camera. Orbiting drops back to the free camera.

camera_speed.description: Scales flying, zooming and panning, as in the 3d view.

camera_mode.description: free: Unreal Editor's camera (drag turns and walks, right-drag looks, WASD flies, Alt+drag orbits). orbit: drag orbits the selection's centre, else the point under the press, else the focus point; middle-drag pans; right-drag and the wheel dolly toward it. Switching keeps the camera where it is.

view_mode.description: What the picture shows: lit (the render), unlit (base colour, no lighting), wireframe (edges over black), collision (only the prims with UsdPhysics CollisionAPI, as their collision shapes, in a flat tint). A stage without colliders shows lit.

environment.description: What lights the stage beyond its own lights: stage (its own lights; a stage without any gets a plain dome), sky (one of NVIDIA's dynamic procedural skies with a sun, named by sky; RTX only: Storm shows the HDRI instead) or hdri (an image-based light, one of the 3d view's HDRIs, named by hdri). Composed over the stage in the viewer, never written to the file; kept across stages. The skies and the HDRIs are fetched on first use into the user's Specto folder; snap reports what shows, the fetch's progress and a note when it is not the choice (the sky or the HDRI not fetched yet).

sky.description: The dynamic sky when environment is sky: clear, cirrus, light or heavy cumulus, overcast, night, or the textured cloudy sky (67 MB of textures, fetched last).

hdri.description: The HDRI when environment is hdri (and what stands in for the sky under Storm or while the sky is fetched): one of the 3d view's Poly Haven environments (web/3d/environments.json).

ground.description: With a sky: the floor of the preview scene the skies ship with (10 x 20 m, its top at height 0, in the stage's units), under the stage. Off by default.

time_of_day.description: The sky's time of day in hours (0-24): moves its sun and the light of the viewer's sun with it, live. null: the sky's own.

cloudiness.description: The sky's cumulus cover, 0 (none) to 1 (solid), live. null: the sky's own.

haze.description: The sky's atmospheric haze, 0 (clear) to 1 (milky), live. null: the sky's own.

selected.description: The item key of the stage shown (default: the picked item, else the first).

max_pixels.description: Cap on rendered pixels (view size x device pixel ratio).

spp.description: Samples per pixel per frame in path-tracing mode.

panels.description: The side panels' {collapsed, width} by name (VIEW, PRIMS).
